description: Begins accepting incoming TCP connections on a server port, handling both plain and SSL protocols. Uses Boost.Asio for asynchronous operations and dispatches new connections to the protocol detector.
Detects whether an incoming connection is plain or SSL by examining the initial bytes, then dispatches to the appropriate handler (PlainHTTPPeer or SSLHTTPPeer).
Instantiates either a PlainHTTPPeer or SSLHTTPPeer based on the detected protocol, passing the socket and connection details to the peer object.
Starts the session for a plain HTTP peer by spawning an asynchronous read loop to process incoming HTTP requests.
Starts the session for an SSL HTTP peer by spawning an asynchronous SSL handshake, then proceeds to read HTTP requests.
Performs the SSL handshake for a new connection, sets up timers, and on success, begins reading HTTP requests.
Processes an incoming HTTP request, checks if it should be handed off (e.g., for protocol upgrade), and writes a response or continues processing.
Processes an incoming HTTP request on an SSL connection, checks for handoff (such as protocol upgrade), and writes a response or continues processing.
Upgrades an HTTP session to a WebSocket session by creating a new WSSession-derived object (PlainWSPeer or SSLWSPeer) and returning it.
Handles the protocol upgrade request, calls session.websocketUpgrade(), creates a WSInfoSub for subscription management, associates it with the session, and starts the WebSocket session.
Begins the WebSocket session, performing the protocol handshake and starting the asynchronous read/write loop.
Sets WebSocket options, installs control callbacks, starts timers, and initiates the asynchronous WebSocket handshake and read loop.
Handles the result of the WebSocket handshake; on success, disables the close-on-timer flag and starts reading messages from the client.
Initiates an asynchronous read operation to receive the next WebSocket message from the client.
Handles the completion of a read operation, passes the received message to the handler (ServerHandler::onWSMessage), and consumes the buffer.
Parses the incoming WebSocket message as JSON, validates it, and if valid, dispatches it for processing; if invalid, sends an error response back to the client.
Processes a valid WebSocket session message, executes the requested operation, serializes the result, and schedules it to be sent to the client.
Sends a prepared message (typically a JSON result) to the client over the WebSocket connection.
Serializes a JSON message into a stream buffer and sends it to the associated WSSession for delivery to the client.
Queues a message for delivery to the client, enforces the ws_queue_limit, and initiates the write process if the queue was previously empty.
Begins writing the next message in the queue to the WebSocket stream asynchronously.
Handles completion of a write operation, determines if more data remains to be sent, and either continues writing or finalizes the message.
Finalizes the sending of a message, removes it from the queue, and if more messages are queued, starts the next write.
Closes the WebSocket connection, either immediately or after all queued messages are sent, using the specified close reason.
Marks the current operation as complete and initiates the next read operation to continue processing messages.
